parent_verified_opposing_conjecture.source: Faustin Adiceam and Ioannis Tsokanos, Visibility properties of spiral sets, arXiv:2111.01843; MJCNT11(2),149-159 (2022)
parent_verified_opposing_conjecture.quote: By contrast, the existence of a spiral set which is a dense forest remains an open question. As a matter of fact, the authors conjecture that there is no such set but have not been able to establish this claim.
parent_verified_opposing_conjecture.definition_check: Spiral sets use arbitrary spherical sequences. Finite density is the origin-ball lim sup condition, automatically met by spiral sets. Definition1.4 dense forest requires finite density and one visibility function for all start points and directions; it imposes no uniform-discreteness or Delone condition.
parent_verified_opposing_conjecture.consequence_inference: If the forest proof is correct and no earlier construction exists, it settles the stated existence question affirmatively in the plane and refutes the authors' unrestricted nonexistence conjecture. Tevet2025 proved only the constant-angle Fermat case negative.

parent_primary_checks.read_scope: Definitions and main Theorems 1-2; Further Questions; references
facts: General spiral directions are arbitrary; Fermat spirals have one constant angular increment.
Limits use escaping translations only; Theorem 1 retains affine translates of closed subgroups.
Theorem 2 characterizes lattices for a fixed badly approximable angle; it does not give the union over all angles.
Further Questions conjectures existence of a general spiral dense forest and explicitly leaves every-covolume-pi-lattice realization open.

parent_primary_checks.read_scope: Theorem1.3, Corollary1.4, absolute-winning intersection properties, Theorem2.2
facts: Badly approximable reals are absolutely winning; countable intersections retain the property.
Global quasisymmetric homeomorphisms preserve absolute-winning sets.
